summary: Updates the IANA considerations for the Layer Two Tunneling Protocol, describing how values for its registries should be assigned. It is a Best Current Practice and invites suggestions for improvement.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3438 changes how IANA assigns values in several L2TP registries. It uses expert review for the listed values and says reviewers should look for a document that defines the value and active implementation work.

questions: what did rfc 3438 change for l2tp registries
what does expert review check for l2tp values
which l2tp assignments use expert review
subtitle: Updates the review procedures for assigning values in L2TP registries.

tldr.problem: Some L2TP registries used assignment procedures that delayed values needed for implementations, even though their number ranges had many unused values.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3438 changes specified L2TP registry procedures to Expert Review and tells designated experts to check for a defining document and active implementation development.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3438 is a Best Current Practice that updates the IANA assignment guidance for L2TP.

today: RFC 3438 is a Best Current Practice for L2TP IANA registration procedures and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why L2TP Registry Rules Changed
sections.content:
L2TP defines several numeric registries maintained by IANA. The ranges described here run from 0 to 65,535, and the largest number allocated in any one range at the time was 46. The RFC says the ranges were not expected to run out.

Some values needed by implementations had been used in vendor-specific form while formal documents were being prepared. The memo says that can leave products supporting both vendor-specific and IETF values indefinitely.
sections.plainLanguage: Several L2TP lists had many available numbers, but the assignment process could hold up values needed during implementation work. The memo changes the review rules for selected lists.

sections.title: Registries Using Expert Review
sections.content:
Further Control Message AVP values and Message Type AVP values are assigned upon Expert Review instead of IETF Consensus. Further StopCCN and CDN Result Code values and General Error Codes are also assigned upon Expert Review instead of their previous procedures; the General Error Code procedure changes from First Come First Served.

For Expert Review, the designated expert should approve a value only when a document clearly defines it and there is active implementation development. Criteria for L2TP values not named in this memo remain unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: Experts review requests for the registries named in the memo. They look for a clear definition and evidence that implementation work is active.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content: RFC 3438 is an Internet Best Current Practice that updates the L2TP IANA registration criteria. It focuses on assignment procedures and states that it has no security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: This Best Current Practice changes selected L2TP number-assignment procedures. It does not change the L2TP message protocol itself.

references.text: Townsley, W., Valencia, A., Rubens, A., Pall, G., Zorn, G., and B. Palter, "Layer Two Tunneling Protocol (L2TP)", RFC 2661, August 1999.
